name: veil
description: Data exfiltration guard for AI coding agents. Bare `veil` is hook mode: it reads one Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Grok or GitHub Copilot pre-tool hook payload on stdin and prints that protocol's allow/deny decision. Subcommands include read-only discovery, diagnostics, Seatbelt sandbox launch, and brokered metadata processing, plus `install`/`uninstall` for the managed Claude hook entries.

invocation.output_mode: hook decision JSON on stdout in hook mode; JSON with --json on subcommands, human text otherwise

options.name: describe
options.description: Print this operator manifest (identical to `capabilities --json`) and exit 0

options.name: schema
options.description: Print the JSON Schema for hook-mode stdout (the permission decision) and exit 0

options.name: robot_triage
options.description: Deprecated alias of `veil doctor triage --json`

options.name: version
options.description: Print the veil version and exit 0

commands.name: capabilities
commands.description: Emit this machine-readable contract (same document as --describe).

options.name: json
options.description: Emit the contract as JSON

commands.name: robot-docs
commands.description: Print the agent quick-start guide (`robot-docs guide`).

commands.name: operator
commands.description: Discover the authorized spine tools configured in [spine] authorized_tools by running each tool's own --describe. Distinct from this manifest.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON

commands.name: test
commands.description: Predict whether one path would be allowed or denied by the read-decision pipeline. Decides on the path only; file contents and message bodies are not read. With --json the output is a veil.path-decision.v1 document.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit the path inspection as JSON

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain allowlist, protected-pattern and pack matches for one path. Decides on the path only; file contents and message bodies are not read. With --json the output is a veil.path-decision.v1 document.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit the path inspection as JSON

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Scan a directory tree and classify each file path. Decides on paths only; file contents and message bodies are not read. With --json the output is a veil.path-decision.v1 document.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit scan results as JSON

commands.name: sandbox
commands.description: Compile the merged config's protected paths into a macOS Seatbelt profile, or launch a command confined by that profile with a session-scoped metadata broker.

options.name: print_profile
options.description: Print the generated Seatbelt profile to stdout; compiler warnings go to stderr

options.name: dry_run
options.description: Compile and report rule coverage and limitations without printing the profile or applying confinement

arguments.name: command
arguments.description: Command and arguments after `--`; runs under Seatbelt with the broker outside confinement

commands.notes: Loading merged config may migrate a legacy user config. Relative protected patterns are rooted at the current project directory. Glob matches are a filesystem snapshot; newly matching paths require recompilation. Hook-only built-in path classifiers and pre-existing hardlink aliases are not covered by this profile. It does not restrict network access or revoke read-capable file descriptors opened before confinement. The broker socket is private to the session, and broker output is scanned before return.

commands.name: exec
commands.description: Run an authorized spine tool through the active session broker, or directly with the same authorization and output scanning when no broker socket is active.

arguments.name: args
arguments.description: Typed tool arguments; never parsed as shell text

options.name: persist
options.description: Keep this call's derived-registry entry usable after the harness session ends. Goes before the tool name; a --persist after it belongs to the tool

commands.notes: Denied raw-output flags, shell metacharacters, unknown tools, oversized requests, arguments that reach veil's state directory, and detector findings are refused. Broker calls are bounded and audited with input/output hashes. Each delivered result appends one record to the derived registry. It registers stdout, and any file a direct-mode call newly made under --out or --output, only when the detectors pass it and it repeats no text of a protected file; the rest is reported on stderr as 'not registered as derived'. Output is still delivered when it is not registered.

commands.name: derived
commands.description: Report on the derived registry (~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl): the content hashes veil exec registered, which let a Read or Grep of a file with the same bytes through where a protected-path rule would deny it.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: verify only: the file to hash and look up

options.name: json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON

commands.notes: `derived verify` exits 0 when a record with a valid MAC registers the file's content and 1 otherwise. It does not say whether the current session may use that record. From a hooked session, a Bash call that names a protected path is judged as a read whichever command names it, this one included.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON

commands.name: config
commands.description: Show the merged active configuration (system, user, project, environment layers).

options.name: json
options.description: Emit merged config as JSON

commands.notes: Loading config may migrate a legacy user config to ~/.cmdrvl/config/veil/config.toml.

commands.name: audit
commands.description: Show recent audit log entries. Lines that are not audit entries are skipped and counted, not an error.

options.name: json
options.description: Emit recent audit entries as JSON

options.name: validate
options.description: Instead of listing entries, count the audit log's lines by kind (current veil.audit.v2, legacy, unparseable) and list the first 20 unparseable line numbers; takes no --class

options.name: class
options.description: Only entries of one class: egress (a command that sends a protected path off the machine), or a reason_class: direct_read, argv_path, dynamic_path_unresolvable, mcp_argument (a path handed to an MCP tool in its arguments), script_too_large_to_inspect (a script an interpreter was asked to run that veil did not read), redirect_write (a redirection that would overwrite or add to a file veil would not let the command read, or would write into veil's own protected paths)

commands.name: replay
commands.description: Re-evaluate saved Bash, Read, and Grep tool inputs under the current policy and report decision flips. Requires [policy] audit_inputs = true for replayable entries; paths are hashed and entries are skipped when input capture is disabled.

options.name: audit
options.description: Audit JSONL path; defaults to the configured audit path

options.name: since
options.description: Replay entries since Unix seconds or a duration such as 30d

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Inspect config, audit path and guard-hook health without writing; every JSON form is a cmdrvl.doctor.v1 report. `doctor --json` is mode health; `doctor capabilities --json` is mode capabilities (its `contract` is this document); `doctor triage --json` is mode triage (with next_actions). Exits 0 healthy, 1 unhealthy. Says `enforcement: hook-only (advisory; parser-based)` (human form) and carries an `enforcement` object (health JSON): veil is a hook that reads the text of a tool call, and nothing in it enforces an OS sandbox. Deprecated aliases kept for compatibility: `doctor health [--json]`, `doctor --robot-triage` and top-level `--robot-triage` (same document as `doctor triage --json`).

options.name: json
options.description: Emit doctor health as JSON

options.name: robot_triage
options.description: Deprecated alias of `doctor triage --json`

commands.name: install
commands.description: Install the managed veil PreToolUse hook entries (Read, Grep, Bash, mcp__.*, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) into Claude settings (~/.claude/settings.json, or VEIL_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH). Only Read, Grep and Bash are required by operator preflight.

commands.name: uninstall
commands.description: Remove only the veil-owned PreToolUse hook entries from Claude settings.

0.meaning: success, or a hook allow/deny decision was rendered

1.meaning: doctor reported an unhealthy state (an error finding), including `doctor --json`, `doctor triage --json` and the `--robot-triage` alias; or `derived verify` found the file not registered; veil has no other verdict

2.meaning: usage error, malformed or empty hook payload, configuration error, guard preflight refusal, or a path command (test, explain, scan) that could not produce a decision; under --json the path commands print a veil.path-decision.v1 error document on stdout

env_vars.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
env_vars.description: Locates the legacy user config that is migrated on first use

env_vars.name: VEIL_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH
env_vars.description: Override the Claude settings file inspected and edited by doctor/install/uninstall

env_vars.name: VEIL_HARNESS
env_vars.description: Override agent harness detection: claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, cursor or plain

env_vars.name: VEIL_POLICY
env_vars.description: Default policy mode: deny, warn or log

env_vars.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
env_vars.description: Set by Claude Code. A direct-mode veil exec records it, and only a Read or Grep from that session uses the entry unless it was made with --persist

side_effects.notes: Hook mode appends one audit record per evaluated path to the audit log when audit_log is enabled; every record carries enforcement: hook (a hook decided, which is advisory and parser-based; no sandbox is enforced). veil exec appends to the audit log and to the derived registry in ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/, and creates that registry's MAC key there on first use. install/uninstall edit Claude settings. config may migrate a legacy user config. All other commands are read-only. veil never writes to the witness ledger.

hook_mode.stdin: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Grok or GitHub Copilot pre-tool hook payload JSON
hook_mode.stdout: protocol-specific permission decision JSON (see `veil --schema`). For a Claude Code Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit call veil only refuses writes to its derived registry and key; for any other file it prints nothing (no decision)
hook_mode.bare_invocation: stdin that is a terminal or empty exits 2 immediately with discovery guidance

composition.role: pre-tool guard that keeps raw sensitive files out of agent context
canonical_chain: dcg blocks destructive Bash before commands execute
veil blocks raw Read/Grep/Bash exfiltration while allowing authorized spine subprocesses
airlock attests derived artifacts before they cross a model boundary
pack seals boundary manifests and downstream evidence
agent_rules: Do not bypass veil by reading protected files directly; run authorized spine tools instead.
Use veil operator --json to inspect authorized tool configuration after guard preflight is healthy.
Use airlock when derived artifacts are ready to cross the model boundary.
